title: Can a grid of nine numbers have average 10 in every line?
description: A question from the book asks for a three by three grid of nine different numbers in which every row, column and diagonal has an average of ten. The video turns the average into a line total, builds a grid by shifting every number of a known grid, and then changes some numbers to get another grid.
teaching_notes: One idea: an average of ten over three numbers means a line total of thirty, and adding the same number to every cell adds three times that number to every line. Watch for students who check only the rows and forget the columns and the two diagonals.

source: Figure it Out (more on mean and median, question 1)
video_script.why: The child must meet eight averages at once, and a shift of every number moves every line total together.
video_script.substitution: Turn each average into a line total of thirty, and move a known grid by adding the same number to every cell.
video_script.anchor: an empty three by three grid with its three rows, three columns and two diagonals marked as eight lines
video_script.payoff_line: The grid works, and other grids work too

final_answer.value: 7, 12, 11 / 14, 10, 6 / 9, 8, 13 works; yes, other grids also work
final_answer.spoken: the grid with seven, twelve, eleven, then fourteen, ten, six, then nine, eight, thirteen works, and yes, other grids also work

hold_back: Answer: 7, 12, 11 / 14, 10, 6 / 9, 8, 13 works; yes, other grids also work
never_show: the finished grid labelled as the answer before the answer beat
maths_rules: average 10 over 3 numbers: line total = 10 x 3 = 30
start grid 2, 7, 6 / 9, 5, 1 / 4, 3, 8: every row, column and diagonal adds to 15
add 5 to every cell: each line has 3 cells, so each line total rises by 3 x 5 = 15, to 30
(ii) swap across the main diagonal: 7, 14, 9 / 12, 10, 8 / 11, 6, 13 changes 6 cells; all 8 lines still add to 30
video_script.design: One idea: every line adds to thirty, and shifting every cell shifts every line. The grid stays from ground to the end of the idea part.
open_questions: The grid is 3 by 3 as the book figure shows; the figure is not in the extracted text.

narration: <bookmark mark='total'/>Step one, the line total. The sum is the mean multiplied by the count. Ten multiplied by three is thirty.

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Step five, check all eight lines. The rows add seven, twelve and eleven, then fourteen, ten and six, then nine, eight and thirteen. Each total is thirty.
<bookmark mark='cols'/>The columns add seven, fourteen and nine, then twelve, ten and eight, then eleven, six and thirteen. Each total is thirty too.
<bookmark mark='diag'/>The diagonals add seven, ten and thirteen, and eleven, ten and nine. Both totals are thirty. The swapped grid has the same eight totals.
